epics.title: Document Content-Hash Deduplication & Duplicate Merge Migration
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator uploads documents into CRIE, I want duplicate files detected via content SHA-256 and existing duplicates merged losslessly, so that the knowledge base never accumulates redundant document rows and immediately surfaces already-extracted records for review or correction.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 0% duplicate document rows created on identical file re-upload and 100% foreign-key link preservation during legacy duplicate merge
epics.tocConstraintRef: Unchecked document ingestion creating redundant IDs and fragmenting extracted contingent, faculty, and curriculum links
requirements: R1: Compute and persist content_sha256 (with normalized filename and extracted text-size fallback signature) in crie_document_engine.py and the SQLite documents table on every document ingestion.

R2: Enforce duplicate detection in the crie_assistant_api.py upload flow so re-uploading a document with a matching hash does not create a new row and returns deduplicated=true with the original document ID.

R3: Include the list of structured DB records already extracted from the matched document (enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, rup_curricula) and an actionable prompt offering to update or correct those records in the deduplicated upload response.

R4: Provide a transactional, idempotent migration and cleanup script with pre-merge backup verification that merges existing duplicate document IDs 1, 10, and 11 into a single canonical document ID without losing foreign-key links across structured tables.
R5: Handle empty or unreadable files, hash-lookup failures, and concurrent duplicate upload races gracefully with clear error feedback and zero partial or orphaned DB writes.

R6: Verify across unit and integration tests that re-uploading an existing PDF creates no new document row, returns deduplicated=true with the original ID, and preserves all linked records after merging IDs 1, 10, and 11.

slices.title: Add content_sha256 schema and lookup helpers
slices.jtbd: When implementing document schema updates for this epic, I want content_sha256 and normalized file-signature columns indexed in SQLite, so that duplicate detection is deterministic and fast across all uploaded documents.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the SQLite documents table schema, When the schema migration initializes, Then columns for content_sha256, normalized_filename, and text_content_size exist with an index on content_sha256.
Given an existing document record without a hash, When the backfill helper runs, Then content_sha256 is computed deterministically from the stored document content without altering existing primary keys.
Given a lookup query by SHA-256 or normalized filename and text size, When a matching row exists, Then the repository returns the canonical document record and its linked structured table counts.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Missing unique content fingerprint column and index on the documents table
slices.sixSigmaMetric: < 5 ms P95 hash-lookup query latency on SQLite documents table

slices.title: Merge legacy duplicate documents 1, 10, and 11
slices.jtbd: When implementing legacy cleanup for this epic, I want an idempotent transactional migration script that merges duplicate document IDs 1, 10, and 11 with pre-merge backup verification, so that all extracted records and foreign keys remain intact under one canonical document ID.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a SQLite database containing duplicate document IDs 1, 10, and 11 with linked rows across structured tables, When the migration script executes, Then it creates a pre-merge backup snapshot, verifies restore readability, and reassigns all foreign keys to the single canonical document ID inside one atomic transaction.
Given a simulated constraint failure mid-merge, When the transaction rolls back, Then zero rows or links are lost and the database remains in its exact pre-migration state.
Given the migration script is executed a second time, When duplicate IDs are already consolidated, Then the script exits cleanly as a no-op with zero errors.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Foreign-key referential integrity risk across multi-table duplicate document rows
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% foreign-key link retention and 0 orphaned child records post-merge

slices.title: Implement hash deduplication in engine and upload API
slices.jtbd: When implementing upload deduplication for this epic, I want crie_document_engine.py and crie_assistant_api.py to detect matching hashes before insertion and return existing extracted records with an update offer, so that duplicate uploads never pollute the registry and guide the user directly to existing data.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an uploaded PDF whose SHA-256 matches an existing document in SQLite, When POST upload in crie_assistant_api.py processes the file, Then no new row is inserted into documents and the response returns deduplicated=true, the original document_id, the extracted DB records, and an offer to update or correct them.
Given two concurrent upload requests for the same new PDF, When both hit the upload endpoint simultaneously, Then unique-hash conflict handling ensures exactly one document row is created and the second request resolves cleanly with deduplicated=true.
Given an empty or corrupt PDF upload, When ingestion fails in crie_document_engine.py, Then the API returns a structured 4xx error message and rolls back any partial DB changes.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Duplicate document insertion path in upload endpoint bypassing content fingerprint check
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0% duplicate rows persisted across 100 consecutive re-upload and concurrency trials

slices.title: Verify hash deduplication and duplicate merge suite
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA verification for this epic, I want unit and integration tests covering hashing, re-upload deduplication, and legacy ID 1/10/11 merging, so that duplicate prevention and lossless data consolidation are continuously verified.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given unit test fixtures for identical bytes, whitespace-variant filenames, and corrupt files, When the hashing and normalization suite runs, Then identical content hashes match deterministically and corrupt inputs fail cleanly without DB writes.
Given an integration test database seeded with duplicate IDs 1, 10, and 11 and linked trainee/faculty/curriculum rows, When the cleanup migration runs, Then all links resolve to one canonical ID with zero data loss.
Given an already-uploaded PDF re-submitted to the crie_assistant_api.py upload endpoint, When the integration test inspects the DB and response payload, Then documents row count is unchanged and the response contains deduplicated=true, the original document ID, and its extracted records.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Lack of automated regression checks for duplicate re-uploads and multi-table merge integrity
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% pass rate across deduplication unit and upload/migration integration tests

epics.title: Interactive Structured DB Record Inspection & Correction
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator uploads or selects a registered CRIE document, I want to view a structured card of extracted contingent, faculty, and curriculum records and correct fields via chat or table with revision logging, so that inaccuracies in SQLite are fixed immediately and reflected in every subsequent AI response.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% SQLite update accuracy and immediate next-turn agent reflection for corrected trainee, faculty, and curriculum records
epics.tocConstraintRef: Manual inability to inspect and fix parsed SQLite records from documents without direct database access
requirements: R1: Define a shared API contract and typed DTO schemas for listing document-linked records (enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, rup_curricula), applying field updates, confirming deletions, querying revision logs, and returning structured validation errors.

R2: Extend crie_persistent_memory.py with document-scoped CRUD repository methods (supporting registry IDs 1-11 and new uploads) and a SQLite revision audit table logging table name, record ID, field, old value, new value, and timestamp.

R3: Implement REST CRUD endpoints in crie_assistant_api.py for viewing and correcting structured records with field-level validation, transactional revision logging, confirmation requirements for destructive deletes, and non-destructive validation errors that preserve submitted input.

R4: Implement agent tools and response formatting so uploading a file or requesting a registry document displays a structured card of recognized DB records and executes natural-language correction commands (full name, specialty, study/funding basis, faculty assignment, curriculum hours) directly in SQLite.
R5: Ensure subsequent assistant dialogue turns immediately query and cite updated SQLite fields from crie_persistent_memory.py without stale cached values.

R6: Build a responsive, WCAG 2.1 AA compliant UI record card and inline editor for mobile and desktop displaying recognized DB rows with visible save/error feedback, preserved unsaved edits on failure, and explicit confirmation before destructive deletions.

R7: Verify across unit, integration, and E2E tests that selecting or uploading a document (IDs 1-11) and correcting an enrolled trainee record via dialogue or UI persists to SQLite and appears in the next assistant answer.

slices.title: Define structured record CRUD and revision contract
slices.jtbd: When implementing the shared contract for this epic, I want typed request/response DTOs for document-linked records across enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula, so that backend endpoints, agent tools, and UI record cards build against one unambiguous interface.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the three structured domain tables (enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, rup_curricula), When the contract specification and DTO module are defined, Then request/response schemas cover list-by-document, partial field patch, confirmed delete, and revision history entries.
Given invalid field values or missing confirmation flags on destructive actions, When error response schemas are specified, Then structured field-level validation errors return exact field keys and messages so client inputs can be preserved.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Divergent payload shapes between chat agent cards, REST API, and frontend table editor
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% schema alignment between Pydantic API models and frontend TypeScript/JS DTOs

slices.title: Add persistent memory CRUD and revision audit log
slices.jtbd: When implementing storage persistence for this epic, I want crie_persistent_memory.py to expose document-scoped CRUD operations and a SQLite revision log table, so that every trainee, faculty, and curriculum edit is atomic and auditable.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid document ID (including registry IDs 1-11), When the repository queries structured records, Then it returns normalized rows from enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula linked to that document.
Given a field correction on any structured record, When the update method executes in SQLite, Then the target column updates atomically and a corresponding row is inserted into the revision audit table with old value, new value, field name, and UTC timestamp.
Given a nonexistent record ID or invalid column name, When an update is attempted, Then the repository rejects the operation cleanly without modifying any rows.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Lack of unified write and audit-trail methods in crie_persistent_memory.py
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of record mutations paired with an immutable SQLite revision log entry

slices.title: Implement CRUD endpoints in assistant API
slices.jtbd: When implementing API endpoints for this epic, I want crie_assistant_api.py to expose validated CRUD routes for document-linked structured records, so that both users and internal services can inspect and correct extracted data reliably.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a GET request for a document ID (1-11 or newly uploaded), When the endpoint responds, Then it returns all linked records grouped by table along with recent revision metadata.
Given a PATCH request updating trainee full name, specialty, funding basis, faculty binding, or curriculum hours, When validation passes, Then SQLite is updated with a revision entry and HTTP 200 returns the updated record.
Given a validation failure or missing confirmation token on DELETE, When the API rejects the request, Then HTTP 4xx returns structured error details without altering stored data or discarding client payload context.
slices.tocConstraintRef: No HTTP surface for reading or mutating extracted structured table rows by document ID
slices.sixSigmaMetric: < 100 ms P95 CRUD API response latency with 0 unhandled 5xx validation errors

slices.title: Add agent record card output and chat correction tools
slices.jtbd: When implementing conversational record editing for this epic, I want agent tools that render recognized record cards and apply dialogue correction commands directly to SQLite, so that administrators can fix parsed entries naturally in chat and see updates immediately in the next reply.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a newly uploaded document or a user request referencing a registry document (IDs 1-11), When the agent responds, Then it outputs a structured card listing the extracted records from enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, or rup_curricula.
Given a chat command instructing the agent to correct a trainee field, faculty assignment, or RUP hours, When the correction tool executes, Then it writes the change to SQLite via crie_persistent_memory.py, logs the revision, and confirms the exact updated field to the user.
Given a follow-up question in the next dialogue turn about that trainee or document, When the agent generates its answer, Then it queries fresh SQLite state and cites the updated value rather than stale conversation memory.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Static prompt context preventing agent tool writes from updating subsequent dialogue answers
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% immediate SQLite-to-next-turn consistency on chat correction commands

slices.title: Build accessible record card and inline table editor UI
slices.jtbd: When implementing frontend interaction for this epic, I want a mobile-friendly, accessible record card and inline editor for extracted DB rows, so that users can review and adjust trainee, faculty, and curriculum fields with clear feedback.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a document upload or selection in the UI on mobile or desktop viewports, When recognized records are returned, Then an adaptive card/table renders all fields cleanly without horizontal overflow and meets WCAG 2.1 AA (keyboard operable, visible focus, labelled controls, 4.5:1 contrast).
Given a user edits a field and submits, When the save succeeds or fails, Then visible status feedback is shown immediately and any validation or network error preserves the user's unsaved edits for retry.
Given a user clicks delete on a record row, When the action triggers, Then an explicit confirmation modal/prompt is required before sending the destructive request.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Absence of visual record inspection and inline correction interface in chat/registry view
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0 WCAG 2.1 AA critical violations and 100% unsaved-edit preservation on failed submit

slices.title: Verify interactive DB correction test pyramid
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA verification for this epic, I want unit, integration, and E2E tests covering CRUD endpoints, revision logs, chat correction tools, and UI card flows, so that end-to-end record accuracy is guaranteed.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given unit tests for field validators, revision audit logging, and natural-language correction tool parsing, When the suite runs, Then all valid mutations pass and invalid edits or unconfirmed deletes are rejected.
Given an integration test selecting registry document IDs 1-11 and issuing a trainee correction command in dialogue, When SQLite and the subsequent agent turn are queried, Then the DB column reflects the new value and the agent's next reply uses it.
Given an E2E browser test on desktop and mobile viewports, When a user inspects a document card, edits a field inline, and triggers a simulated validation error, Then edits are preserved, valid saves persist to SQLite, and accessibility/keyboard checks pass.
slices.tocConstraintRef: End-to-end regression risk across UI, API, agent tool, and SQLite persistence layers
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% pass rate across unit, API/agent integration, and browser E2E test layers

epics.title: Live DB Registry Guidance & Prompt-Jargon Purge Across Assistant Agents
epics.jtbd: When a user asks the CRIE assistant how to upload, edit, or use documents, I want responses completely free of internal prompt-engineering jargon and grounded in live SQLite document counts and clear UI instructions, so that users understand the exact system state and workflow without confusion.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 0 prompt-engineering jargon leaks and 100% live SQLite document/record count accuracy in file-workflow replies
epics.tocConstraintRef: System prompts leaking internal prompt-engineering terminology instead of reporting live DB registry state and UI steps
requirements: R1: Implement a live SQLite registry summary query returning concrete uploaded documents (titles, IDs, order categories such as residency and postgraduate admission orders) and exact extracted record counts across enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula, including a clean empty-registry message.

R2: Wire live registry summary injection into crie_assistant_api.py agent context assembly with graceful DB-error fallback so temporary storage failures never expose raw tracebacks or internal prompt terminology.

R3: Refactor system prompts and response guards in crie_smart_consultant.py, crie_thought_agent.py, and crie_autonomous_agent.py to prohibit internal prompt-engineering terminology (such as reply-slot and system-prompt jargon in any language).

R4: Ground assistant answers about uploading, editing, and using files in live SQLite document/record counts plus a clear 3-step interface workflow: file attachment button -> automatic DB table parsing -> reviewing and correcting fields in dialogue or table.

R5: Verify via unit and integration tests that asking how to send files to correct data yields zero prohibited slot/prompt jargon, cites real SQLite document statistics, and presents the 3-step workflow guide.

slices.title: Build live DB registry document and count summary query
slices.jtbd: When implementing registry introspection for this epic, I want a read-only SQLite summary query aggregating uploaded documents and extracted row counts across contingent, faculty, and curriculum tables, so that assistant agents always report real backend state.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given populated documents, enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula tables in SQLite, When the registry summary query runs, Then it returns each uploaded document's ID, title, category, and exact extracted record counts per table.
Given an empty documents table, When the summary query executes, Then it returns zero counts and an explicit empty-registry state flag without raising exceptions.
slices.tocConstraintRef: No consolidated read query for per-document and per-table extracted counts
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% count agreement with direct SQL COUNT(*) queries across all three tables

slices.title: Inject live registry summary into agent runtime context
slices.jtbd: When implementing runtime context wiring for this epic, I want crie_assistant_api.py to supply fresh DB registry summaries to consultant and autonomous agents on every turn with safe fallback handling, so that file-guidance replies are always up to date.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an incoming user chat turn in crie_assistant_api.py, When the agent context is assembled, Then the latest SQLite document inventory and extracted row counts are passed into the agent runtime.
Given a simulated SQLite read error during summary lookup, When context assembly catches the failure, Then it logs the error and supplies a safe user-facing unavailable-stats notice without leaking tracebacks or prompt jargon.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Stale or missing backend registry statistics during agent prompt assembly
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0 unhandled exceptions and < 20 ms context-assembly overhead per turn

slices.title: Purge prompt jargon and add live workflow guidance in agents
slices.jtbd: When implementing agent prompt and guardrail updates for this epic, I want crie_smart_consultant.py, crie_thought_agent.py, and crie_autonomous_agent.py to ban prompt-engineering jargon and answer file-workflow questions with live DB stats and 3-step UI instructions, so that users receive accurate, plain-language guidance.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given updated system prompts and output guardrails across crie_smart_consultant.py, crie_thought_agent.py, and crie_autonomous_agent.py, When a response is generated, Then internal prompt-engineering terms (reply slot, system prompt, and equivalent jargon) are strictly prohibited and stripped/rewritten if detected.
Given a user question about uploading, editing, or using files, When the assistant composes its answer, Then it lists real uploaded documents from SQLite with extracted contingent, faculty, and curriculum record counts and states the 3-step guide (attach button -> auto-parse to DB tables -> review/edit in chat or table).
slices.tocConstraintRef: Hardcoded prompt templates containing internal slot terminology instead of dynamic user guidance
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0% prohibited jargon occurrences across 50 adversarial file-help prompt variations

slices.title: Verify jargon purge and live DB guidance behavior
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA verification for this epic, I want unit and integration tests validating the jargon guardrail, live DB summary formatting, and end-to-end file-help agent replies, so that regressions in assistant terminology or state grounding are caught immediately.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given unit tests for the jargon-prohibition guardrail and live DB summary formatter across populated and empty DB states, When the suite runs, Then prohibited slot/prompt terms are blocked and exact document and table counts are formatted accurately.
Given an integration test submitting a user query asking how to send files to correct data across consultant, thought, and autonomous agent paths, When the responses are inspected, Then zero slot or system-prompt jargon appears, real SQLite document names and record counts are cited, and the 3-step upload-parse-edit workflow is present.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Untested prompt changes risking regression to internal slot terminology
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% pass rate on jargon-absence and live-stat citation assertions
